The whole-archive facades are the only consumer-linkable construction today (thin re-export facades fail the consumer static link and the core cannot satisfy references to mangled internals); the court pins the exact partition profile (transform-phase allocator/register/deregister/loader unobserved, keepBlanks 56 vs oracle 41) so any silent architectural change is caught.

amendment_scope: 1. DEFAULT-ALLOCATOR UB FIX (R-000178): the pre-Z.3 default allocator routed through Rust's std::alloc with fabricated Layouts — default_free deallocated every pointer with Layout::from_size_align_unchecked(1,1) and default_realloc passed the requested NEW size as the OLD allocation layout; both are invalid-layout UB under the Rust allocator contract. The default is now plain libc malloc/realloc/free/strdup (upstream 2.15.0 globals.c defaults: xmlFree=free, xmlMalloc=malloc, xmlMallocAtomic=malloc, xmlRealloc=realloc, xmlMemStrdup=xmlPosixStrdup), untracked exactly like the oracle (xmlMemUsed/xmlMemBlocks/xmlMemSize == 0 under the default, byte-identical), with the debug-named surface (xmlMemMalloc/xmlMemFree/xmlMemRealloc/xmlMemoryStrdup and the *Loc variants) keeping the registry + counters exactly like upstream's MEMHDR debug allocator (verified byte-identical). xmlMemDisplay/xmlMemDisplayLast/xmlMemShow/xmlMemoryDump are upstream-faithful no-ops (2.15.0 removed the feature); xmlMallocAtomicLoc no longer zeroes (upstream xmlMallocAtomicLoc -> xmlMemMalloc is a plain allocation). NEW ALLOCATOR-DEFAULT-001 differential court: many sizes, zero-size, grow/shrink realloc, realloc-to-zero (glibc frees+returns NULL), realloc/malloc failure (SIZE_MAX), strdup/NULL handling, free(NULL), direct exported-variable calls, 100k alloc/free churn, xmlMemSize/xmlMemUsed/xmlMemBlocks exactness, no-op display entry points — byte-identical SHA-256 with the oracle. The valgrind memory-safety sweep is not executable in this environment (valgrind 3.25.1 SIGILLs inside the dynamic loader on every binary including /bin/true — a toolchain incompatibility, recorded as unavailable in the receipt).

2. ABI-FUNCTION-SIGNATURE HARDENED (fail-closed + oracle-isolated + two fingerprints): the oracle plane compiles with ONLY /usr/include/libxml2 + the default system paths and the candidate plane with ONLY repo include/ — the previous court passed candidate -I paths into the oracle parse, so nested #include <libxml/tree.h> could resolve from the candidate tree (oracle contamination). Every resolved include origin is recorded (clang -H) and cross-universe resolution is a finding. A header clang cannot parse is a finding (the old court silently dropped unparseable headers — it never measured namespaces.h/transformInternals.h, which upstream only includes after a prerequisite; they are now parsed through a documented wrapper). A candidate-declared function without a measured Rust extern "C" fn is a finding unless classified (DATA / ASM shim / macro-generated shim / candidate-header auxiliary). Full accounting: 71/71 oracle + 73/73 candidate headers parsed, 0 failed, 0 include-origin findings, 0 unmeasured, silent_omissions = 0. Two fingerprints per symbol: SOURCE_PROTOTYPE_FINGERPRINT (canonical/desugared base type, pointer depth, pointee const/restrict, typedef identity, FULL function-pointer signature — a (void*)->void callback can no longer compare equal to an (xmlNodePtr,int)->int callback, variadic, arg count, return type, calling convention) compared oracle-vs-candidate, and MACHINE_ABI_FINGERPRINT (ABI class, width, SIGNEDNESS, pointer depth, struct-by-value identity, callback ABI, variadic; size_t==usize==c_ulong at the machine level) compared oracle-vs-candidate AND candidate-vs-Rust. Result: 3259 compared, 0 findings.

3. SIGNATURE-DRIFT CLOSURE (25+ real candidate divergences the old lossy normalization could not see): signedness/width (xmlBufferGrow/xmlBufferShrink int->unsigned int incl. oracle buf.c semantics, xmlDictSize unsigned int->int, xmlDictSetLimit/xmlDictGetUsage unsigned int->size_t, xmlOutputBufferGetSize int->size_t with oracle 0-on-error semantics), wrong returns (xmlXPathCastBooleanToNumber int->double, xmlCheckVersion int->void, xmlInitThreads int->void), wrong arity (xmlValidateAttributeDecl 4->3 args; the 4th xmlNodePtr elem did not exist upstream), wrong fn-pointer typedefs (xsltPreComputeFunction was void(*)(style,inst) instead of xsltElemPreCompPtr(*)(style,inst,xsltTransformFunction); xsltTopLevelFunction carried a phantom void* data arg — both fixed in headers + Rust types), an invented xmlTextReaderGetAttributeIndex API (not in the oracle header/source; removed from the candidate header), pointee identity drifts (xmlListFront void*->xmlLink*, xmlXPathCompile/xmlXPathFreeCompExpr void*->xmlXPathCompExpr*, xsltGetExtInfo void*->xmlHashTablePtr, htmlCreateFileParserCtxt void*->htmlParserCtxt*, char vs xmlChar on xmlURIEscapeStr/xmlOutputBufferGetContent/xmlXPathNewCString), const drifts (xmlGetNsList/xmlGetParameterEntity/xmlGetLastError/xmlBufferContent), enum-vs-int spelling (xmlBufferSetAllocationScheme/xmlValidateAttributeValue now use the enum typedefs), and the xmlAttributeTable/xmlElementTable/xmlEntitiesTable/xmlNotationTable typedef identities (aliased to struct _xmlHashTable exactly like the oracle). xmlBuffer.h declarations moved into tree.h positions matching the oracle.

4. SAFETY PROOF SCOPES (11.2 goal demonstrated): CUSTODIAN-COMMENTARY-DRIFT now GATES the verdict on zero unaccounted safety sites. The census classifies every unsafe block as local-proof (SAFETY comment in the block window), enclosing-proof-scope (the enclosing fn's doc documents a # Safety contract, or an explicit // SAFETY-SCOPE: <ID> marker), classified-generated (macro-generated code, or modules carrying a module-level SAFETY-SCOPE marker — the mechanical export-registry modules), or unaccounted (verdict gate: 0). Result: 5235/5235 unsafe blocks accounted (local 2514, enclosing-proof-scope 2720, classified-generated 1) and 1811/1811 unsafe functions accounted (1795 documented + 16 scope-covered). The rustdoc gate (RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features) is now part of the receipt and passes; 10 pre-existing rustdoc defects (broken intra-doc links, unescaped #[no_mangle], an unclosed HTML tag, a bare-URL lint) were fixed.

5. xslHandleDebugger CLASSIFICATION CORRECTED: reclassified from the old 'residual R-000176' label (R-000176 is FIXED) to HEADER_DECLARED_ORACLE_DSO_ABSENT — declared in the oracle transform.h but NOT exported by the system libxslt.so.1 (verified: nm -D has no such symbol, only xsltGetDebuggerStatus); current-oracle requirement N/A. xsltCleanupSourceDoc (transformInternals.h) is likewise oracle-DSO-absent and classified the same way.

6. DOCUMENTATION TRUTH: README/Cargo.toml counts regenerated (1183 tests, 79 FIXED / 3 OPEN, 82 residuals, alpha.36); the Y census adds ALLOCATOR-DEFAULT; R-000131's narrative sealed to the Z.3 state (default = untracked libc, debug surface = tracked registry, display fns = no-ops); R-000177 reframed as the Phase-12 machine-enforced DSO-boundary-lint target.

residuals.open_disposition: R-000157 is OPEN/UNRESOLVED: a REAL current executed-platform gap (iconv/ICU-only encodings vs the Iconv+ICU-enabled 2.15.3 oracle) whose closure requires implementing an iconv/ICU backend — a future implementation work item, explicitly NOT waived. R-000168 is the bounded unexecuted-platform evidence obligation (Windows/macOS/BSD/32-bit runtime), documented per-obligation in atlas/PLATFORM_SURFACE_ATLAS.json. R-000177 is the documented cross-DSO state partitioning of the whole-archive facades, pinned by the DSO-STATE-COHERENCE court and carried as the deliberately-open Phase-12 architectural target (machine-enforced DSO boundary lint). CORRECTED ACCEPTANCE: surface/evidence completeness is sealed for the executed platform; one known current implementation residual (R-000157) and the unexecuted-platform evidence obligation (R-000168) remain open and are explicitly deferred, and one bounded packaging divergence (R-000177) is accepted and court-pinned. There is no claim that open candidate-parity residuals = 0 — R-000157 is a genuine current executed-platform implementation gap.
